binders: A measurable space Omega with a probability measure mu.
Natural numbers n and k with n>0.
A family X_{j,i}: Omega -> Real indexed by blocks j in Fin(2k+1) and within-block positions i in Fin(n).
Real parameters sigma, epsilon, and delta.
hypotheses: Every X_{j,i} is measurable and belongs to L2(mu).
The random vectors omega |-> (X_{j,i}(omega))_{i in Fin(n)} are mutually independent as j ranges over the 2k+1 blocks.
Within each fixed block j, the variables X_{j,i} are pairwise independent for distinct i.
Every X_{j,i} is identically distributed with the reference variable X_{0,0} under mu.
The number of blocks satisfies 2k+1 >= log(1/delta)/(2(1/4)^2), equivalently 2k+1 >= 8 log(1/delta).
conclusions: Let M_j(omega) = (1/n) sum_{i in Fin(n)} X_{j,i}(omega), and let Med(omega) be the kth order statistic of the 2k+1 values M_j(omega). Then mu({omega : epsilon <= |Med(omega) - E_mu[X_{0,0}]|}) <= delta.
mathematical_definitions: Each block estimator is the arithmetic mean M_j = n^{-1} sum_i X_{j,i}.
The aggregate estimator is the median of the odd family (M_j)_{j in Fin(2k+1)}, implemented as the entry at sorted position k.
The center is the Bochner integral E_mu[X_{0,0}], which is also the common expectation because all variables are identically distributed and integrable.
The failure event uses a closed threshold: absolute error greater than or equal to epsilon.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For 2k+1 mutually independent blocks of n real observations on one probability space, where all observations share a common distribution with variance sigma squared, every observation is measurable and square-integrable, and observations within each block are pairwise independent, form the mean of each block and take the median of those block means. If n is at least 4 sigma squared divided by epsilon squared and 2k+1 is at least 8 log(1/delta), with epsilon positive and delta strictly between zero and one, then the probability that this median differs from the common mean by at least epsilon is at most delta.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The within-block assumption is only pairwise independence, not an explicit jointly independent family; across blocks, however, the whole Fin(n)-valued block vectors are mutually independent.
The statement fixes exactly 2k+1 blocks and hence an odd sample of block means; it does not cover an arbitrary number of repetitions directly.
The sample-size lower bound has the explicit constant 4, and the repetition bound has the explicit constant 8 after simplification.
No hypothesis requires sigma>=0; only sigma^2 occurs, so replacing sigma by -sigma leaves the assumptions and conclusion unchanged.
The conclusion bounds the event |error|>=epsilon, including equality, rather than only |error|>epsilon.
The common mean is not introduced as a separate parameter but is the integral of X_{0,0}; identical distribution and L2 membership make it the mean of every observation.
The probability is expressed by converting the measure value to Real. Because mu is a probability measure, the event measure is finite and this conversion is nonpathological.
The assumptions n>0, epsilon>0, and 0<delta<1 prevent division by zero in the operative sample mean and displayed lower bounds.
ambiguities: The packet exposes Tuple.sort through a graph-equivalence implementation but does not state its ordering theorem inline; the local definition and real linear-order dependency indicate that LocalDef002 is the kth sorted value, hence the median of 2k+1 inputs.

The constructors/axioms of the external predicates IsProbabilityMeasure and IdentDistrib are not expanded in the packet, so their conventional mathematical readings are taken from their displayed library roles and types.
